problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(1,1),(0,0),(-1,1),$ and $(0,2).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(0,-1)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(-1,0)$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The quadrilateral $Q$ is mapped to the quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ has vertices $(2,-5),(3,-6),(4,-8),$ and $(3,-7).$ Which of the following are vertices of $Q?$

- $(-5,-2)$
- $(-6,-3)$
- $(-8,-4)$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${Q}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $Q$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0-(-1)}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -6 & -8 & -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -6 & -8 & -7 \\ -2 & -3 & -4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(-5,-2),(-6,-3),(-8,-4),(-7,-3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
